title: Final Fantasy
subtitle: the sixteen numbered games, their sequels, and the VII remake line
blurb: 22 games — about 832 hours of story, 661 of it the sixteen numbered ones, with Revelation still to come.
paceLabel: the sequels and the remake line
notes: A new Final Fantasy number is a new world, a new cast, a new story — there is no continuity between the numbered games, which is the franchise's whole deal. Start anywhere. The tier-2 rows are the exceptions: direct sequels and the VII remakes, which do need their parent.

HowLongToBeat main-story figures — no side content, no completionist padding. The two MMOs get the same treatment and it undersells them: XI's figure is its base story, and XIV's is A Realm Reborn alone, under a decade of expansions.

1 is the sixteen numbered games, about 661 hours. 2 is the branches off them — X-2, the XIII sequels, and the VII remake line. A finish date paces the numbered spine; the checkbox under the bar adds the branches.

VII Remake and Rebirth are not the usual kind of remake — they retell VII across three games, and they land best with the original played first. The third part, Revelation, is due on 8 April 2027, so the line is here unfinished.
Hours and dates from HowLongToBeat, verified by name; the list itself checked against Wikipedia's series page, and Revelation's release date against its own article.
